candidate_relations.reason: Angiolymphoid hyperplasia with eosinophilia has a different epithelioid endothelial and inflammatory morphology.
No spindle-cell component or cavernous thrombotic spaces support spindle cell hemangioma.
The acquired progressive bland lymphatic proliferation is not characterized as a vascular malformation.
Ecchymosis describes the peripheral bruise-like appearance but not the underlying lymphatic neoplasm.
HHV-8 negativity, bland endothelial cells, and low proliferation argue against Kaposi sarcoma.
The lesion lacks the lobular capillary architecture of pyogenic granuloma.
A large infiltrative lymphatic plaque is not a cherry angioma.
A KSHV-negative vascular tumor is broadly compatible but does not identify benign lymphangioendothelioma.
Multifocal lymphangioendotheliomatosis is related by lymphatic lineage but conflicts with this solitary benign plaque.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: multifocal systemic rather than solitary benign lesion

candidate_relations.reason: The biopsy shows vascular channels rather than a lymphoid neoplasm.
There is no chronic lymphedema or malignant endothelial atypia to support Stewart-Treves syndrome.
Bland endothelial cells, absent mitoses, and low Ki-67 argue against angiosarcoma.
The biopsy demonstrates lymphatic vascular channels rather than dermatofibroma.
The chronic bland lesion without systemic infection is not bacillary angiomatosis.
Hemosiderin deposition alone does not make the infiltrative lymphatic lesion a hemosiderotic hemangioma.
Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma is a distinct typically small lesion and does not match this large infiltrative plaque.
Hemangioma is a broad benign vascular label but omits the lymphatic endothelial identity and infiltrative pattern.
The lesion lacks glomeruloid architecture and the systemic context of glomeruloid hemangioma.
There is no verrucous epidermal surface or deep congenital malformation pattern of verrucous hemangioma.
No limb arteriovenous malformation or venous hypertension supports Stewart-Bluefarb syndrome.
